AK.key_factor: Every October poll, including Republican sponsors, still had Peltola ahead on first-choice votes.
AK.reasoning: Peltola took 49.5% in the primary and leads first choices by about two points. Ranked-choice transfers from two minor Republicans, plus the late spoiler investigation, can erase that lead, which is why this is the closest race. Her money advantage and the national climate leave her just ahead in the final round.

FL.key_factor: Polls through the final week, including Democratic surveys, show Moody ahead by four to eight points.
FL.reasoning: Florida voted Republican by 13 points in 2024, and Nixon's democratic-socialist profile limits crossover appeal. The national Democratic environment and heavy outside spending on her behalf tighten the race into the high single digits rather than a landslide. Early voting does not show a surge large enough to overturn Moody's lead.

IA.key_factor: The freshest polls have Hinson slightly ahead in a state Trump carried by 13 points.
IA.reasoning: Nonpartisan polls are essentially tied, while Republican pollsters put Hinson up about two. Turek is better funded in a hostile year for the president's party, but an open seat in a state this red still breaks narrowly to the Republican as undecided voters settle. The Libertarian vote keeps both major candidates under 50%.

KS.key_factor: Late Emerson, Washington Post, and CNN polls all show Hamilton leading the incumbent.
KS.reasoning: Kansas remains heavily Republican, so a lead for a first-time candidate has to be discounted. Marshall's patient-lawsuit scandal and Trump's rally defense of those suits are specific enough, and the late nonpartisan polls consistent enough, to make Hamilton a modest favorite by about two to three points.

ME.key_factor: October polls from CNN, Marist, Suffolk, The Washington Post, and several Republican firms have Jackson ahead.
ME.reasoning: Collins beat her polls by a wide margin in 2020, so a two-point Jackson lead is not secure. This year's surveys are much more one-sided, Trump is deeply unpopular in a state he has never carried, and Jackson's edge held through the debates. With only two candidates on the ballot, ranked-choice voting does not change the outcome.

MI.key_factor: Nearly every October poll, including Republican-sponsored surveys, shows El-Sayed leading Rogers.
MI.reasoning: Rogers lost Michigan's other Senate seat by 0.3 points in 2024, and El-Sayed barely won a progressive primary. Those risks already appear in the surveys, which still give him a steady three-to-five-point lead in a Democratic year. Minor-party candidates in the low single digits do not overturn that lead.

MN.key_factor: Flanagan leads every recent poll, including Tafoya's own campaign survey and other Republican-sponsored polls.
MN.reasoning: Minnesota leans Democratic, the national environment leans further that way, and the lieutenant governor is a conventional favorite against a first-time candidate. Tafoya's celebrity and Trump's late endorsement make the margin closer than a Klobuchar race, landing around seven points rather than a toss-up.

NC.key_factor: Cooper, a two-term governor, leads Whatley by roughly eight to twelve points in virtually every poll.
NC.reasoning: No survey in the dossier, including Republican pollsters, has this race inside five points. Whatley has never won elected office, Republican outside groups cut a large planned buy, and Cooper's fundraising dwarfs his. North Carolina's slight Republican lean cannot close a gap this wide.

NE.key_factor: Most recent polls, including one sponsored by Osborn, still have Ricketts ahead by a point or two.
NE.reasoning: Osborn's 46.5% against Deb Fischer in 2024 shows he can consolidate the anti-Republican vote with no Democrat on the ballot. A better national environment pulls him close, but Ricketts is the incumbent in a state Trump won by 20 points, and the remaining undecided voters should favor him.

NH.key_factor: Saint Anselm, New Hampshire's benchmark poll, has Pappas ahead of Sununu by seven points.
NH.reasoning: The Sununu name and heavy outside Republican spending keep this from being a blowout in a state that just elected a Republican governor. Every public poll since the September primary, including Republican sponsors, still has the sitting congressman up by about five to seven points.

OH.key_factor: Brown leads Husted in nearly every October poll, including several commissioned by Republicans.
OH.reasoning: Brown lost Ohio by 3.6 points in 2024 while running well ahead of the Democratic presidential ticket. The midterm climate, his large fundraising edge, and a steady polling lead are enough to take the seat back. Ohio's rightward shift and a couple of Republican-leaning pollsters keep the race inside three points.

SC.key_factor: Even a tied Siena poll, in a state Trump carried by 18 points, leaves the Republican ahead once undecided voters break.
SC.reasoning: Graham is an unelected appointee who won a fractured runoff and has been badly outspent, which is why the race is far closer than South Carolina's usual Republican margins. State fundamentals and the higher-quality local polls still point to a Graham win of about four to five points.

TX.key_factor: A broad set of October polls puts Talarico narrowly ahead of a scandal-damaged Paxton despite the state's Republican lean.
TX.reasoning: Texas polls have overstated Democrats before, and the newest Quantus survey has Paxton up one. The balance of polling, Paxton's impeachment baggage, the bitter Cornyn primary, and Talarico's $146 million haul still make the Democrat a slight favorite in a strong Democratic year.

upset_watch.why: Peltola leads on first choices, but ranked-choice transfers from the other Republicans and a late investigation into a same-name spoiler can still erase that edge.
